title: land's undelivered warning names the failed gate's first error line, and a check-trailers refusal by name
goal: bl_land.last_push_failure names the first error line of the failed gate's output, not the last line kg_sync prints (kg_sync.py:646), and names a check-trailers failure, which has no (exit N), instead of falling back to kbgit.py sync exit 1, as the backlog.md and tools.md text says

clauses.clause: bl_land.last_push_failure names the first error line of the failed gate's output, not the last line kg_sync prints (kg_sync.py:646)
names a check-trailers failure, which has no (exit N), instead of falling back to kbgit.py sync exit 1, as the backlog.md and tools.md text says

gates.question: Which side picks a failed gate's first error line for land's undelivered warning: land's reader of the delivery log (bl_land.last_push_failure, reading the gate's output block there), or the sync script that writes the gate's summary line?
options: land's reader of the log, the sync script untouched
the sync script, which writes the first error line into the gate's summary
gates.recommendation: land's reader of the log, the sync script untouched
gates.answer: land's reader of the log, the sync script untouched

notes: Found at the SP-kwi4ilty review. Premise run 2026-10-12 on a planted distill.log: a gate line '  gate check-trailers origin/main..HEAD: FAILED: commits=3 bad=1' before 'apply --push: kbgit.py sync exit 1: nothing pushed to main' gives 'kbgit.py sync exit 1: nothing pushed to main' (PUSH_GATE needs '(exit N)'), and '  gate tests.py (changed): FAILED (exit 1): 1 failed, 40 passed in 9.1s' gives that summary line, the last output line kg_sync prints, not the first error. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 16 of 19, "Land snags: gate answers committed by the tool, link touches, stale-touch reads, generated coverage files and the undelivered warning"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
